title: OTLP conditional forwarder: dynamic routing to Tempo and legacy Jaeger with schema translation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build an OTLP forwarding component that conditionally routes incoming traces to either Tempo (native OLTP/OTLP path) or a legacy Jaeger ingestion gateway. The forwarder must: preserve sampling decisions, translate span attributes and tags between canonical schema and legacy jaeger tags, support per-tenant routing rules, handle mTLS and credential rotation, and expose health/backpressure signals for the console. Acceptance criteria: 1) Routes by tenant header and sampling hint with deterministic, testable policy; 2) Provides correct Jaeger envelope translation for span IDs, trace flags, and legacy tag mappings; 3) Gracefully degrades to a fallback queue when downstream is overloaded and emits SLO metrics; 4) Includes end-to-end tests and a dashboard in Grafana showing routing distribution, error rates, and downstream latencies.
comments: 2026-03-05 - Kickoff: scoped core routing rules and schema translation matrix. Identified three tenant patterns: modern (OTLP native), legacy (jaeger endpoint), and hybrid. Decided to read X-Tenant-ID and X-Sampling-Hint for routing.

2026-03-07 - Prototype: implemented a lightweight routing layer in the ingest gateway to inspect OTLP ResourceSpans for 'service.name' and headers. Initial prototype forwards directly to tempo:14250 and to jaeger:14268 depending on rule.

2026-03-08 - Trade-off discussion: discussed per-request vs sticky routing. Chose per-request deterministic routing for simplicity and auditability; added a sticky cache as an opt-in optimization for high-volume tenants.

2026-03-09 - Backpressure: added a circuit-breaker and token bucket per-destination. If Jaeger queue exceeds watermark, we now fall back to disk-backed dead-letter queue and emit metric 'ingest.forwarder.jaeger.queue_fallback'.
2026-03-11 - Security review: initial keys rotation flow reviewed with security. Need explicit KMS integration for service account rotation (follow-up).
2026-03-12 - QA: end-to-end test harness passing against tempo mock and a jaeger v1.21 collector. Found one mapping bug for 'db.system' -> 'db.type' legacy tag; fixed in branch.
2026-03-12 - Next: prepare PR and add console panels for routing and per-tenant latency heatmap. Coordinate with release lead for runtime-1.20 cut.

Design (Ravi Singh) - requested trace-tag mapping matrix and sample payloads for legacy services; added mapping doc.
Security (Maya Lopez) - requested KMS proof-of-concept for credential rotation and mTLS policy; flagged as security_review_required.
QA (Jordan Lee) - requested chaos tests that simulate intermittent tempo latency and verify deduplication semantics.
decisions: Deterministic per-request routing using header + resource attributes rather than sticky only.
Use translation layer for jaeger envelopes rather than altering upstream clients to preserve backwards compatibility.
Introduce a bounded disk-backed fallback queue for the Jaeger route to avoid data loss on transient overloads.
Expose routing telemetry (counts, latencies, queue depth) to Redwood Console for oncall and SLO monitoring.
changes: Add routing rule config to tenant profile in control plane (follow-up ENG-271001 for tenant config UI integration).
Implement KMS-backed credential rotation flow and add to operator runbook.
Extend existing tracer contract tests to include legacy jaeger tag validation and trace-id endianness checks.
Add canary rollout with percent-based traffic split before making routing config public.
